items.note: The lemon hero band has a 96px headline, a pink CTA and five different thick stickers ringing it (parcel, receipt, button, ticket, spool), some cropped by the edges. Below it are an ink-framed filter bar, cards with a drawn object for each item, pink price flags and a black footer: clearly the reference's language. The hero objects are smaller and sparser than the reference's 200px+ coins, and the CTA is a small single button where the reference has a big CTA paired with a bordered search.

The hero stacks well. Stickers are cropped at the band edges like the reference's phone pricing band, the headline is large and the CTA is full-height. The filter box keeps the 48px ink-hairline character. The category pill row drops its last item off the edge with no scroll cue, which is looser than the reference's tidy phone chrome.

Matches the reference's dark appearance: black ground and bar, a pink cart block, a white current pill, and a lemon hero band with its stickers unchanged. Filter bar and card bodies sit one step lighter, so depth now reads correctly (the rc.1 inversion is fixed).

Same hero as light on a black bar with a pink cart block. The band and stickers are unchanged, and the raised filter box is lighter than the black ground, matching the reference's dark treatment. Spacing below the CTA is a little loose but the screen holds together.

Lemon header band with breadcrumb and section-size title, then a framed buy panel with a notched flag, option boxes and a pink submit: good chrome. The product drawing is a flat, single-outline object enlarged to about 600px, so its 2px ink reads thin. It has no back or side band and is cut off by the frame's bottom edge. The image is much cruder than the reference's chunky die-cut objects.

Band header, framed image and framed buy panel stack cleanly at the reference's 48px control scale. At this size the drawing's outline reads closer to the reference's weight, though it is still a flat outline without the thick construction.

Correct dark layering: lemon band unchanged, black ground, lighter raised buy panel, and the pink flag keeps its outline. It shares the light page's oversized flat drawing, thin at this scale and cut off by the frame's bottom edge.

Dark phone page: unchanged lemon band, black ground, a lighter raised panel with a visible hairline, and the flag intact. The drawing sits on its band-colored box as the spec requires. Composition matches the light phone page.

Same strong chrome as the tote page: lemon band, framed buy panel, flag, ruled detail list. The sweater drawing is a large flat outline whose hem runs off the bottom of the frame, with thin ink for its size. The size options mark the selection with a 2px ink border and a pink radio dot instead of the reference's pink selected border.

The breadcrumb wraps to two lines in the band, but title, lead and seam read well. The sweater fits its frame at phone size with an ink weight close to the reference's. Panels keep the 1px ink frame on paper.

Dark layering is correct and the band and flag are unchanged. The enlarged flat drawing, cut off by the frame, is the weakest part, and the selected option still uses an ink outline rather than the pink selected border.
Phone dark page: lemon band, marigold image box and a lighter raised panel on black, with a visible pink flag. The drawing fits its frame. The page reads as the reference's dark appearance.

Periwinkle header band with a thick receipt sticker at the trailing edge, cropped by the side only. Below it, a dashed white empty box holds a distinct open-parcel drawing, one sentence and a pink action, as in the reference's dashed empty state. The empty box is very wide for its little content.

Band, receipt sticker (cropped at the side, well over 60% visible), dashed empty box with the parcel drawing and a full-width pink action stack cleanly. It is close to the reference's phone app screen, which has a band header, a dashed empty state and a black footer.
Unchanged periwinkle band and sticker, a raised dashed box on black, and a pink cart block in the bar, matching the reference's dark rules. The dashed edge is faint at 35% white but still reads.

Same composition as light on a black ground with a lighter dashed box. The parcel keeps its ink outline because it sits on the raised field, as the spec asks. The footer separates from the ground with a hairline.

findings.summary: On the product page, the item's drawing is one flat outline enlarged to fill a roughly 600px image box. Its 2px ink reads hairline-thin at that size, it has no back or side band, and on desktop the frame cuts the object off at the bottom. The reference's objects stay chunky die-cut stickers at any size: a heavy outline relative to the object, a visible thick edge, and the whole object inside its field or cropped only deliberately at a band edge.
findings.promptFix: A drawn item image is a sticker at every size. Build it with the four-step thick construction (back, side band, face, inner strokes), not as a single outline. Keep the object within 55–70% of the image box's width, centred, with at least 8% clear ground on every side, so the frame never cuts it. When the box is wider than 320px, draw the object at that size instead of scaling up a small drawing, and keep the ink outline at 3px for a large detail image so it stays as heavy as on a card.

findings.summary: The hero sticker ring is sparser and smaller than the reference's. Only two of the five objects reach large size, the button and ticket are small fragments in the bottom corners, and the primary action is a compact single button. The reference sets 200px+ objects close around the headline and gives the CTA a large block paired with a bordered search.

On the buy panel, a selected option is marked with a 2px ink border and a pink radio dot, and the disabled decrement is a grey-filled box. The reference marks selection with the pink selected border on a radius.sm box and never uses grey fills.
On phones the category pill row inside the filter box pushes its last category off the edge with no scroll cue.
